inventory_method: Read from the working tree at the commit below; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md does not exist in this repository, so no claim here is taken from it. Every § reference is a citation copied out of a code docstring, not a verified spec reading.

runtime.notes: firebase-admin and MetaTrader5 are NOT installed in this environment. aureon/storage/firebase_service.py:62 imports firebase_admin lazily and raises RuntimeError when absent (verified: main_review.py fails at that line). The emulator test suite uses google-cloud-firestore 2.31.0 directly (tests/failure_injection/conftest.py:70). Also present: pandas 3.0.6, numpy 2.4.6, pytest 9.1.1, ruff 0.16.8. pyproject.toml declares mt5 and discord as optional extras.

services.name: observer

steps: outbox worker.flush() — deliver what the previous run queued, before adding to it (main_observer.py:268)
log any still-undelivered rows; the worker retries (main_observer.py:272)
_backfill(symbol, timeframe) per symbol/timeframe, chronologically through the live engine (main_observer.py:281, 309)

services.notes: imports_mt5 is false in the literal sense: main_observer.py contains no `import MetaTrader5`. It imports aureon.data.mt5_provider, which imports MetaTrader5 lazily inside a function (aureon/data/mt5_provider.py:108) — hence runs_on windows. Detection evaluation runs INSIDE this process (main_observer.py:130 _track_outcomes, :145 _advance_evaluations, :156 _persist_evaluations); there is no separate evaluator service or entrypoint.

services.name: executor

steps: reconciliation.reconcile_all() — repair or fail every request left EXECUTING/PENDING (main_executor.py:91)

services.notes: Both: a Firestore on_snapshot listener on status=='confirmed' (aureon/execution/execution_worker.py:346) plus a poll loop (:375) whose interval is AUREON_EXECUTOR_POLL_SECONDS, default 2.0. The poll is described in-code as the actual guarantee and the listener as best-effort.

steps: _reconstruct_offline_excursions() from M1 candles, BEFORE the first poll, only for trades whose stored excursion is empty (main_monitor.py:83, 97)
monitor.startup() — import open positions, close what closed, resolve pending, import external (main_monitor.py:85; aureon/positions/position_monitor.py:117)

services.name: discord

steps: check_configuration() refuses to start without a token or with an empty allowlist; a missing guild id is a loud warning only (main_discord.py:32)

services.notes: startup_recovery.implemented is false because there is no state recovery — only configuration validation. Nothing needs recovering: Discord holds no lease and no in-flight work.

services.name: review
services.notes: Not a loop and not a daemon: a one-shot CLI (`main_review.py daily|weekly`), idempotent and re-runnable for any past period, with scheduling left to cron/systemd (main_review.py:1-24, decision 88). It writes no heartbeat, so /status cannot tell whether reviews are being generated. Cannot be launched in this environment: build_service -> get_client needs firebase-admin, which is absent.

models.name: AureonModel
models.notes: Base for every model. model_config extra='forbid', frozen=False, validate_assignment=True.

models.name: AureonDocument
models.notes: Adds schema_version (default SCHEMA_VERSION = 1). Every stored model below inherits it.

models.name: Detection
models.notes: The only model with frozen=True at the document level (aureon/models/detection.py:87). CLAUDE.md requires detections be immutable.

models.name: PendingOrder
models.notes: There is deliberately no pending_orders collection (decision 9, aureon/storage/paths.py:12); a pending order IS the PENDING trade request.

models.name: DailyReview
models.notes: field_count counts fields declared on this class only; it inherits 18 from ReviewBase + schema_version.

models.name: WeeklyReview
models.notes: Doc id built by aureon/storage/paths.py:weekly_review_doc_id; sorts chronologically as a string.

models.name: SymbolState
models.notes: Carries last_quote: one current snapshot per symbol, overwritten in place (decision 80) — state, not a tick stream.

models.name: SymbolInfo
models.notes: Stored via SymbolRepository although it is an AureonModel, not an AureonDocument, so this document carries NO schema_version field.

state_machines.name: trade_request
bypass_writes_found: aureon/storage/trade_request_repository.py:431 — resolve() only calls assert_trade_request_transition when `current.status is not new_status`. A same-status write with updates/failure_code therefore writes without consulting the table. This is load-bearing by design for EXECUTING->EXECUTING (aureon/execution/execution_worker.py:155 stamps comment_token that way, and the code comment at :418 says an earlier early-return silently dropped it) and for re-entrant PARTIALLY_FILLED. The residual gap: a TERMINAL status can also be rewritten this way — resolve(FILLED, updates={...}) on an already-FILLED request mutates the document even though `filled` has no outgoing edges.
aureon/storage/trade_request_repository.py:176 — create() writes status=REQUESTED with from_status=None. A creation, not a transition; no prior state exists to validate.

state_machines.name: trade
bypass_writes_found: aureon/storage/trade_repository.py:182 — transition() calls assert_trade_transition only when `current.status is not new_status`; a same-status write with updates skips it. CLOSED is terminal, so transition(trade_id, CLOSED, updates={'realized_pnl': ...}) on an already-CLOSED trade rewrites a terminal document's fields.

aureon/storage/trade_repository.py:145 — upsert_open() sets status=OPEN on creation with from_status=None, and deliberately leaves an already-recorded position alone rather than overwriting it. A creation, not a transition.
aureon/storage/trade_repository.py:210 — update_excursion() writes excursion figures without changing status and is deliberately not audited (documented as such at that line).

state_machines.name: control_request
bypass_writes_found: aureon/storage/control_request_repository.py:120 — create() writes status=REQUESTED with from_status=None. A creation, not a transition.
state_machines.notes: resolve() (aureon/storage/control_request_repository.py:189) returns early on an unchanged status BEFORE writing, so unlike the two machines above it has no same-status bypass. It also does not verify the caller holds the lease, where trade_request_repository.resolve does (:410).

state_machines.name: horizon
state_machines.notes: Not in the requested enum list but present in the code. In-memory tracker state, gated at aureon/evaluation/outcome_tracker.py:383 and :388 immediately before each assignment. A COMPLETE horizon is frozen so re-running the tracker cannot change it.

detection_id.notes: agent_version is deliberately EXCLUDED (decision 16, aureon/models/identity.py:66): a patch release re-running over history must upsert the same document, not mint a parallel detection for a candle that happened once. The separator is ASCII unit separator 0x1F, not '|', because event_key legitimately contains '|' (liquidity/breakout emit '{direction}|{level_type}') and with '|' the pairs ('up','a|b') and ('up|a','b') would hash alike (aureon/models/identity.py:28).

comment_token.notes: Deterministic on purpose: an executor that crashed mid-send re-derives the exact token it stamped and reconciliation searches the broker's order/deal history for it. Base32 to avoid case-folding and punctuation risks in a field that round-trips through a broker terminal. 10 chars is well inside MT5's 31-character comment field (decision 5).

identity.account_scope_source: aureon/config/config.py:161 — AUREON_ACCOUNT_SCOPE, default 'primary'. Threaded into AnalysisEngine (account_scope=), TradeRepository(account_scope=) and the detection_id hash. The Phase 1 decisions doc states it must be set before Phase 2 and never changed, because changing it re-keys every detection id and every trade id.

agents.name: ema_cross
agents.notes: The only agent that sets a direction (aureon/agents/ema_cross_agent.py:118). RSI is attached as context and never gates the detection.

agents.name: wick
agents.notes: direction=None (aureon/agents/wick_agent.py:122), so a wick rejection carries no tradeable side despite having a directional name.

agents.name: liquidity
agents.notes: direction is the IMPLIED reversal (aureon/agents/liquidity_agent.py:176): event_key 'up|previous_day_high' carries direction=SELL. Shares one LevelTracker with breakout.

agents.name: breakout
agents.notes: direction=implied (aureon/agents/breakout_agent.py:134). Shares one LevelTracker with liquidity.

pending_excluded_from_reviews.how: Three layers. (1) DetectionEvaluation exposes complete_horizons / pending_horizons / invalid_horizons, and aureon/reviews/aggregate.py:168 folds ONLY complete_horizons into the reached/evaluated counts. (2) A boundary test, tests/boundary/test_architecture_boundaries.py:194, is AST-precise and fails if any file under aureon/reviews reads `.horizons` on anything but a whitelisted receiver — verified to catch `evaluation.horizons`. (3) Every review carries pending_horizons_excluded and invalid_horizons_excluded (aureon/models/review.py:105-107) so the omitted count is reported beside the counted one. aureon/reviews/linking.py:classify returns UNKNOWN (never a miss) for a PENDING or INVALID horizon. Reverting layer (1) to fold pending horizons into the denominator is caught on four horizons by the baseline reconciliation (verified by planting it).

evaluation.notes: There is no separate evaluator service; the tracker runs inside the observer process (main_observer.py:130-170). Rules are frozen once shipped: register() raises if a rule_id is re-registered with a different definition (aureon/evaluation/rules.py:75). The Phase 2 baseline records a finding that these thresholds ($0.03-$0.20 on gold at point=0.01) are reached >=95% of the time in every horizon and that 463/470 path classifications are ambiguous, so they measure the scale rather than the strategy; the sanctioned fix is a new rule_id, never an edit (docs/PHASE2_BASELINE.md).

claim_transaction.notes: CONFIRMED -> EXECUTING only; anything else raises ClaimRejected. Sets executor_instance_id, lease_expires_at (= now + lease_seconds) and execution_started_at inside the Firestore transaction. An expired confirmation is written FAILED_STALE inside the SAME transaction and the refusal is raised by the caller AFTER the commit (:286, :333) — raising inside would abort the transaction and roll the safety write back, leaving the request CONFIRMED and claimable later at a price the human never saw.

confirm_transaction.notes: checks_user_match: aureon/storage/trade_request_repository.py:217 rejects any user_id != requested_by. checks_quote_ttl is false for THIS transaction: it SETS expires_at = now + confirmation_ttl_seconds but does not validate the age of the quote being confirmed. Quote age is gated twice elsewhere — aureon/discord/service.py:353 (check_confirm_press, which re-prompts rather than refusing) and aureon/execution/execution_guard.py:202 (rule_quote_fresh, at execution time). A duplicate confirm is a no-op returning the current document (:212), not a second transition.

execution.guard_notes: 17 rules, run in order by check() (aureon/execution/execution_guard.py:424); EVERY rule must pass and the first refusal wins — order affects only which reason a human is shown. The registered list is itself pinned by tests/unit/test_execution_guard.py:100 test_the_guard_has_all_its_rules_registered, and :312 test_the_guard_is_pure. On success the guard CLAMPS deviation to max_deviation_points and never widens it (:448, test at :216). IMPORTANT: this rule list is inferred, not ratified — docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §41/§56/§57 have never existed in this repository, and docs/PHASE1_DECISIONS.md decision 55 logs all 17 as inferred.

reconciliation.notes: Verified by grep: aureon/execution/reconciliation_service.py contains no call to send_market_order, send_pending_order, cancel_order or close_position. No match before the grace period elapses leaves the request EXECUTING and reports 'no match yet' (:173); only past the grace does it become FAILED_RECONCILIATION (:184). Several broker records matching one token is FAILED_RECONCILIATION / reconciliation_ambiguous rather than a guess (:158, test tests/failure_injection/test_scenarios.py:435). grace_seconds default DEFAULT_GRACE_SECONDS = 120.0 (:53), overridable by AUREON_RECONCILE_GRACE_SECONDS.

execution.magic_source: aureon/config/config.py:164 — AUREON_MAGIC, default 770177 (config field aureon_magic at :72). Passed to ExecutionWorker(magic=), ReconciliationService(magic=), PositionMonitor(magic=) and stamped on every BrokerOrderRequest.
execution.comment_notes: aureon/execution/execution_worker.py:148 sets comment=token on the single BrokerOrderRequest the worker builds; there is no other construction site in aureon/execution. The token is persisted to the request BEFORE the send (:152-166) precisely so a crash leaves reconciliation something to search for.
exactly_once_layers: SendGuard (aureon/execution/idempotency.py:32) registers the request id BEFORE sending and raises AlreadySent on a second attempt in the same process. In-memory only — a dict guarded by a lock — so it does NOT survive a restart.

The durable layer that does survive: the status is written to EXECUTING inside the claim transaction before any send, and claim() refuses anything not CONFIRMED, so a restarted process cannot re-claim an in-flight request.
An unknown broker result leaves the request EXECUTING for reconciliation and never retries (aureon/execution/execution_worker.py:174-190).

positions.close_matching_notes: Closes are matched on mt5_position_id plus the deal's entry type (aureon/positions/deal_reconciler.py:13, :103 summarise_position filters deals by d.position_id). The comment token is used for a different job: finding which REQUEST opened a position, via the entry deal (aureon/positions/position_monitor.py:281-284), and for resolving pending orders (aureon/positions/pending_order_monitor.py:98). So: position_id for closes, comment for attribution.
positions.external_trades_notes: aureon/positions/position_monitor.py:213 — a position whose magic != Aureon's, or with no matching request, is recorded with source=EXTERNAL_MT5 and trade_request_id=None. Observed and reported on, never managed (:25).
positions.excursion_notes: aureon/models/enums.py ExcursionSource. Live via ExcursionTracker.on_quote (aureon/positions/excursion_tracker.py:116); reconstructed from M1 candles via reconstruct_from_candles (:145), used at monitor startup for positions that were open while the monitor was down (main_monitor.py:97). Once a stored excursion is RECONSTRUCTED the tracker keeps that source (:99).
positions.partial_close_notes: aureon/positions/position_monitor.py:406 _apply_partial_closes, with PARTIALLY_CLOSED re-entrant in the state machine (aureon/models/enums.py:400) so 0.25 -> 0.10 -> 0.05 is three closes. PollResult.partially_closed tracks them (:67).

discord.command_notes: Every handler carries @requires_authorization (aureon/discord/bot.py) and defers within three seconds before any Firestore read. The confirm button in aureon/discord/views/confirm_view.py:85 writes trade_requests (confirm) and :177 writes settings (enable). /trading disable takes effect immediately with NO confirmation step, while enable requires a confirming press (decision 84) — the safe direction has no speed bump.
discord.boundary_evidence: tests/boundary/test_architecture_boundaries.py:155 (no MetaTrader5, no mt5_broker, no engine.indicators, no order_send/send_market_order/send_pending_order anywhere under aureon/discord), :287 (cannot import the repositories that write detections, evaluations, sessions or reviews), :321 (BotContext has no broker or provider field or annotation). Verified by grep: zero broker calls in aureon/discord.
discord.confirm_identity_notes: Checked twice, independently. aureon/discord/service.py:338 (check_confirm_press) rejects a press by anyone but request.requested_by — Discord messages are channel-visible, so this is not hypothetical — and aureon/storage/trade_request_repository.py:217 rejects it again inside the confirm transaction, so a UI bypass still cannot confirm someone else's money. Tests: tests/failure_injection/test_scenarios.py:175 test_scenario_c_variant_only_the_requester_may_confirm.

storage.repository_notes: ReviewReader is write-free by construction and is what the Discord BotContext holds instead of ReviewRepository (aureon/discord/context.py:52), so /status cannot overwrite a review. The three money/state repositories use Firestore transactions and write their audit row INSIDE the same transaction (tests/failure_injection/test_scenarios.py:384). ExecutionSettingsRepository.set_trading_enabled does NOT use a transaction: it reads, writes the settings document, then writes the audit row as a separate call (aureon/storage/settings_repository.py:66-92) — see risk_flags.
raw_firestore_calls_outside_storage: aureon/reviews/service.py:89 — self._client.collection(paths.DETECTIONS).stream(). A READ, and an unbounded full-collection scan filtered in Python.

aureon/execution/execution_worker.py:357 — _where(self.repository._client.collection(paths.TRADE_REQUESTS), 'status','==','confirmed') then on_snapshot. A READ, and it reaches into the repository's PRIVATE _client (carries `# noqa: SLF001`).
storage.raw_call_notes: All six are reads; grep for `).set(`, `).update(`, `).delete(` outside aureon/storage returns nothing, so the 'writes go through repositories' half of the CLAUDE.md rule holds. The 'no raw client calls elsewhere' half does not. The existing guard (tests/boundary/test_architecture_boundaries.py:177) only checks that nobody OUTSIDE aureon/storage imports google.cloud.firestore or firebase_admin — it does not check for .collection()/.document() calls on an injected client, so none of these six is caught.

outbox.notes: SQLite with PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and PRAGMA synchronous=FULL (aureon/outbox/local_outbox.py:87-88). delivered_at is set only by mark_delivered, documented and implemented as 'called ONLY after the remote write succeeded' (:138). A failed attempt calls record_failure, which keeps the row undelivered (:148). Rows are never deleted on delivery, only marked; an already-delivered row is never resurrected (:100). Partial index on undelivered rows (:49).

All 31 variables above appear in .env.example.

tests.acceptance_notes: N_REQUESTS = 50 (:34), SEEDS = tuple(range(20)) (:35), each request independently assigned a failure mode from a seeded RNG (:113). Seeds are fixed so a failure replays exactly. Four tests: :104 exactly-once under randomised failure, :155 every valid request executes exactly once (first 5 seeds), :194 no request is ever left EXECUTING after reconciliation, :220 the reconciler never places an order.
tests.requires_mt5_notes: The 'mt5' marker is declared in pyproject.toml:40 but NO test uses it. Nothing in the suite exercises a real MT5 terminal; the MT5-only legs of the Phase 2/4/5/6 gates are unproven (docs/PHASES.md).
tests.skipped_without_emulator: All 101 tests under tests/failure_injection, each reporting 'FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST is not set...' from the session fixture at tests/failure_injection/conftest.py:52. The skip is loud and module-level by design: a green run that proved nothing would be worse than a red one.
tests.run_notes: Plain run 458.74s, emulator run 493.46s. ~6 minutes of each is the 21 tests in tests/replay: test_every_agent_holds_replay_live_parity takes 20.7-23.5s per agent because aureon/engine/levels.py:152 does pandas DatetimeIndex.floor work over a 583-bar window on every candle.

spec_compliance.invariants_source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md DOES NOT EXIST in this repository (docs/ contains only CONTRACTS.md, PHASE0_STATUS.md, PHASE1_DECISIONS.md, PHASE2_BASELINE.md, PHASES.md). §79 could not be read, so the eight invariants below are the non-negotiables enumerated in CLAUDE.md, which is the actual normative list the code was built against. Each is evaluated individually against the code. Every '§' in this file is a citation copied from a code docstring, not a verified spec reading.

invariants.name: A detection never creates a trade; no broker call from observer, agents, engine, evaluation or reviews
invariants.evidence: Two guards, both structural. tests/boundary/test_architecture_boundaries.py:71 fails if any file under aureon/{agents,engine,outbox,data,evaluation,reviews} imports aureon.execution at all (AST-based, so a lazy in-function import is caught); :88 additionally fails on any textual mention of order_send/BrokerInterface/send_market_order/send_pending_order in those packages. Confirmed by grep: order_send appears only in aureon/execution/mt5_broker.py (lines 217, 221, 224, 257, 296).

invariants.name: Execution only from CONFIRMED, via a Firestore transaction that sets the executor lease; unknown broker result reconciles, never retries
invariants.evidence: aureon/storage/trade_request_repository.py:256 claim() refuses any status but CONFIRMED and sets executor_instance_id + lease_expires_at + execution_started_at inside the transaction. aureon/execution/execution_worker.py:174-190: a BrokerError or unexpected exception leaves the status EXECUTING and increments left_executing, never re-sends. aureon/execution/idempotency.py:39 registers the send BEFORE it happens. Reconciliation places no orders (verified by grep and by tests/failure_injection/test_exactly_once_acceptance.py:220). Proven end to end by scenarios A-H and 20 seeds x 50 requests.

invariants.name: All state changes go through assert_transition; never write a status field without it
invariants.evidence: Every genuine status CHANGE is gated: aureon/storage/trade_request_repository.py:225, :292, :317, :434; trade_repository.py:183; control_request_repository.py:148, :192; evaluation/outcome_tracker.py:383, :388. The gap: trade_request_repository.py:431 and trade_repository.py:182 call the assert only when `current.status is not new_status`, so a SAME-status write carrying updates bypasses the table. That path is load-bearing by design (EXECUTING->EXECUTING stamps comment_token; PARTIALLY_FILLED is re-entrant), but it also means a TERMINAL document's other fields can be rewritten — resolve(FILLED, updates={...}) on a FILLED request, or transition(CLOSED, updates={...}) on a CLOSED trade, both write. No test pins terminality against that path.

invariants.name: Money-moving logic depends on BrokerInterface, never MetaTrader5 directly; only mt5_provider.py and mt5_broker.py may import MetaTrader5
invariants.evidence: grep for `import MetaTrader5` across the repository returns exactly two code sites: aureon/data/mt5_provider.py:108 and aureon/execution/mt5_broker.py:105, both inside a function. tests/boundary/test_architecture_boundaries.py:110 enforces the two-module allowlist over every file under aureon/, and :128 separately enforces that both import it LAZILY (module-scope only, not ast.walk), which is what lets the whole suite run on Linux. Both concrete brokers subclass BrokerInterface (aureon/execution/mt5_broker.py:82, fake_broker.py:85).

invariants.name: Every timestamp is tz-aware; MarketTime for stored records; never datetime.now() without tz, never local OS time
invariants.evidence: aureon/models/base.py:43 to_utc() raises on a naive datetime, and UtcDatetime (:30) applies it at validation time, so a naive value cannot reach Firestore. utc_now() (:34) is the single sanctioned clock and returns datetime.now(UTC). grep for datetime.now()/utcnow()/time.time()/date.today() across aureon/, main_*.py and scripts/ finds exactly two calls, both tz-aware: base.py:40 (datetime.now(UTC)) and aureon/data/historical_provider.py:191 (datetime.now(UTC), a fallback when a fixture has no candles). MarketTime validates its zone exists (:104) and derives the market rendering rather than storing it.

invariants.name: Detections are immutable; outcomes live in detection_evaluations; no Detection field encodes future information
invariants.evidence: Detection is the only document model with frozen=True (aureon/models/detection.py:87). Outcomes live in a separate collection keyed {detection_id}__{rule_id} (aureon/storage/paths.py:detection_evaluation_path). Reviewing all 17 Detection fields (:89-122): detected_at is the candle CLOSE ('when this became known'), price is the close price at detection, and indicators/levels/session/sequence are all as-of that candle — none reads forward. The tracker is independently prevented from measuring a detection against its own candle (aureon/evaluation/backfill.py:14-18).

invariants.name: Firestore writes go through aureon/storage repositories only; no raw client calls elsewhere; tick data never goes to Firestore
invariants.evidence: The WRITE half holds: grep for `).set(` / `).update(` / `).delete(` outside aureon/storage returns nothing. The 'no raw client calls elsewhere' half does NOT: six raw read call sites exist outside storage (aureon/reviews/service.py:89, :111, :126, :140; aureon/discord/result_listener.py:66; aureon/execution/execution_worker.py:357, which also reaches into the repository's private _client). The existing boundary test (:177) only checks that nobody outside storage IMPORTS a Firestore SDK, so it catches none of them. Tick data: no ticks collection exists in aureon/storage/paths.py; the one live quote is a single overwritten SymbolState.last_quote field (decision 80), which is state rather than a stream.

invariants.name: Discord never calls the broker and never computes indicators; it reads Firestore and writes only trade_requests, settings.trading_enabled and audit_logs
invariants.evidence: The broker/indicator half is fully enforced: tests/boundary/test_architecture_boundaries.py:155 and :321, plus grep (zero broker calls under aureon/discord). The write scope is BROADER than the sentence allows: Discord also writes control_requests (aureon/discord/commands/control.py:86). That is deliberate and documented — CLAUDE.md's list predates Phase 6, and the boundary test at :251 explicitly names control_requests as how §46/§47 ask for cancels and closes to be requested — but the code and the CLAUDE.md sentence do not match as written. Status is 'partial' for that reason alone, not because of an unsafe capability: the executor still performs the action under the same claim/lease discipline, and Discord never reports the outcome from its own return (decision 85).

mismatches.spec_says: CLAUDE.md line 3 instructs 'Read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (frozen, §94) ... before any change', and every phase prompt and most code docstrings cite it by section number.

risk_flags.what: The 17 execution guard rules — every gate between a human's confirmation and real money — are inferred, not ratified. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §41/§56/§57 have never existed in this repository, so the rule list, its failure codes and its ordering were derived rather than read.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: A missing rule is a money-losing bug that no test can reveal, because the tests were written from the same inference as the code. Every rule present is individually unit-tested and the registered list is pinned, so the risk is not a broken rule — it is a rule nobody knew to write. This should be reconciled against the real section text before a funded account.

risk_flags.what: A same-status write bypasses the transition table, so a TERMINAL document's non-status fields can be rewritten: resolve(FILLED, updates={...}) on an already-FILLED request, or transition(CLOSED, updates={...}) on an already-CLOSED trade, both commit.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: The path exists for a good reason (EXECUTING->EXECUTING must carry comment_token, and an earlier early-return silently dropped it — the code says so at :418), and it cannot change a status. But it can silently overwrite a settled trade's realized_pnl or a filled request's fields, which is exactly the kind of after-the-fact edit that makes P&L and every review built on it unfalsifiable. No test pins terminality against this path.

risk_flags.what: ExecutionSettingsRepository.set_trading_enabled is not transactional: it read-modify-writes the settings document and then writes the audit row as a separate, unguarded call.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: This is the kill switch. Two concurrent toggles are last-write-wins with no read-set check, so a disable racing an enable can be lost. And because the audit write is separate, the switch can flip with no audit row (or an audit row can land for a write that failed) — a gap in the §60 trail on the one setting that decides whether real money can move. Every other money-touching repository writes its audit row inside the same transaction.

risk_flags.what: Six raw Firestore read calls live outside aureon/storage and the boundary guard cannot see them, because it checks SDK imports rather than call sites.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: Today they are all reads, so no client-side money write exists. But the guard that is supposed to prevent one does not actually constrain this shape of code: the next raw call on an injected client could be a .set() and the suite would stay green. The executor's case is worse in kind — it reaches into repository._client, a private attribute, so the repository's write discipline is one attribute access away from being sidestepped. Separately, the three reviews calls are unbounded full-collection scans filtered in Python (documented as a deliberate trade to avoid composite indexes), which is a scaling rather than a safety concern.

risk_flags.what: ControlRequestRepository.resolve does not verify the caller holds the lease, where the trade-request equivalent does.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: A stale executor whose lease expired can still record the outcome of a cancel or close it no longer owns, overwriting the outcome the current holder wrote. The transition table keeps it to one EXECUTING->COMPLETED/FAILED edge, so the blast radius is a wrong reason or detail on a control request rather than a duplicated broker action — but it is an asymmetry with the trade-request path, not a documented decision.

risk_flags.what: SendGuard, the in-process double-send guard, is a plain in-memory dict and does not survive a restart.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: Listed for completeness because it looks like the duplicate-order defence and is not the durable one. The durable layer does hold: the status is written to EXECUTING inside the claim transaction before any send, and claim() refuses anything not CONFIRMED, so a restarted process cannot re-claim in-flight work. Verified by scenario A and by 20 seeds x 50 requests. The residual exposure is a send whose status write succeeded and whose outcome is unknown — which is left EXECUTING for reconciliation by design, never retried.

risk_flags.what: The review service writes no heartbeat and has no loop, so nothing reports whether reviews are actually being generated.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: /status derives liveness from heartbeats/{service} for observer, executor, monitor and discord only (aureon/storage/paths.py:SERVICES). A cron that stops firing is invisible: /status would keep showing the last weekly review it found, with nothing to indicate the review process has been dead for a month. Not a money risk — it is a silent-staleness risk in the surface a human uses to judge the system.

risk_flags.what: No test exercises a real MetaTrader5 terminal; the 'mt5' pytest marker is declared but unused.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: Everything about order placement, fills, partial closes and deal history is proven only against FakeBroker. The MT5-only legs of the Phase 2, 4, 5 and 6 gates are explicitly recorded as outstanding in docs/PHASES.md, so this is a known and disclosed gap rather than a hidden one — but it means no byte has ever been exchanged with a broker terminal, and the MT5Broker payload shapes are unverified.

risk_flags.what: Detections reach Firestore through a durable SQLite outbox on one machine's local disk.
risk_flags.why_it_matters: The 'lost detection' path is well defended in software: WAL + synchronous=FULL, delivered_at set only after the remote write returns, failures kept undelivered and retried, and the observer flushes the previous run's queue before adding to it (main_observer.py:268). The residual risk is not logical but physical — undelivered rows live only in a local file, so losing that disk loses detections that were observed but never delivered, with nothing upstream to replay them from except the broker's own candle history.
